title: T1596 — Search Open Technical Databases
subtitle: This animation shows a fictional recon operation called Operation Quiet Ledger .
aria: Animated diagram: an attacker queries five free public databases (passive DNS, WHOIS, certificate transparency, CDN data, scan databases) about Northwind Freight, assembles a target dossier, and the SOC sees only a DNS anomaly and some scanner user agents. A full written version of all eight steps follows in the page text.

steps.title: Choose the target
steps.caption: The attacker selects Northwind Freight Ltd. and sets a goal: find a quiet way in without touching the company's systems. They open an empty dossier and plan to fill it using only free public sources
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Passive DNS search
steps.caption: The attacker asks a passive DNS service for every name it has seen under northwind-freight.example . The service answers from its own stored records: live subdomains and old IP addresses, including hosts that moved long ago.
steps.defender: none - passive queries never touch the victim's servers.

steps.title: WHOIS lookups
steps.caption: WHOIS queries return registration records. The main domain and two partner domains share a registrant email, so the attacker links them into one family - and collects two staff addresses that were not redacted.
steps.defender: the query is invisible; privacy redaction shrinks what the record teaches.

steps.title: Certificate transparency search
steps.caption: On a CT search site the attacker finds a certificate issued eight months ago for staging.northwind-freight.example - a forgotten test host that appears in no document and no asset list.
steps.defender: monitor certificate transparency logs for your domains.

steps.title: CDN data review
steps.caption: CDN and hosting data show the website sits behind a large content delivery network. One DNS record and one response header hint at the origin server's real address behind that shield.
steps.defender: restrict origin servers to accept CDN traffic only.

steps.title: Scan database search
steps.caption: In internet scan databases the attacker finds three indexed exposures. They include an open RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) port on a branch office, an old VPN appliance banner from 2023, and a camera login page with default-credential hints.
steps.defender: track your external footprint weekly with an external attack surface management (EASM) tool.

steps.title: Assemble the dossier
steps.caption: The attacker merges everything into one page: subdomains and old IPs, staff emails, the forgotten staging host, an origin hint, and three weak services. The next phase now has a shopping list - and the victim logged none of it.
steps.defender: still quiet - your edge logs show zero packets from the attacker.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: SOC retrospective
steps.caption: The SOC reviews the month. The database queries left no trace at all. What did leave traces: a small spike of NXDOMAIN answers in DNS logs and a few scanner user agents on the website - exactly the signals worth alerting on.
steps.defender: alert on NXDOMAIN spikes and known crawler user agents; keep DNS and edge logs for at least 90 days.
